newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey confirms barley export tender cancelled.
newsitem.headline: Turkey confirms barley export tender cancelled.

text.p: Turkey's state grain board (TMO) cancelled a tender to export 150,000 tonnes of feed and 50,000 tonnes of malting barley because of unsatisfactory prices, a TMO official said on Wednesday.
"The tender has been cancelled," said one official. "The prices bid by the participants were not favourable," he told Reuters.
The TMO held a tender on Monday in which five companies -- Cargill, Glencore, Grains & Fourrages, Rotel and Sesos -- gave prices ranging from $121.46 to $133.06 per tonne of feed barley.
Only Glencore bid for the malting barley at the agreed price for feed barley plus $17.
"We do not think we will put out another tender soon for the barley we have. We will think of other means to dispose of it," the official said, without elaborating.
Farm officials said earlier the TMO held about 500,000 tonnes of feed and malting barley, most of it being earmarked for local sales and the remaining for exports.
